solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scheme to have a hundred poles around agricultural territory

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: the poles are said to have something inside them, holding it within their letters

parts.note: a pole, rod or perch is an old unit of length
a scheme is a plan

explanation.surface: A planning scheme in which a hundred surveyor's poles are set out round some farmland.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles here are old units of length, five and a half yards, not posts or Polish people. 'Around' is only a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Croplands are fields given over to growing crops, which is farming territory.

clue.text: Wild ceilidh expelling one Scottish fellow

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the letters run riot into a new order
expelling means throwing something out, so a letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk dancing, taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one, the letter thrown out

explanation.surface: A rowdy Highland dance throws out one of its Scottish guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one I from CEILIDH and rearrange the remaining six letters. A ceilidh is a Scottish dance party.
explanation.definitionFit: Chield (or chiel) is a Scots word for a lad or young man, so a fellow in Scotland.

clue.text: Some grand employer — one has three horses

indicators.note: some of a phrase means only part of its run of letters is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A wealthy boss who keeps three horses in his stable.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside gRAND EMployer.
explanation.definitionFit: A randem is a carriage or team with three horses harnessed one in front of another, like a tandem with an extra horse.

clue.text: A head extraordinarily appreciative when dismissing 4E

indicators.note: extraordinarily suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are put into an unusual order
dismissing sends something away, so those letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
4 is IV in Roman numerals, followed by the letter E

explanation.surface: Someone extraordinarily grateful brushes aside a cross-reference to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: '4E' looks like a reference to a clue numbered 4 across, but there is none: it is Roman IV plus E. Take IVE out of APPRECIATIVE and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Per capita is Latin for 'by heads', meaning for each person, as in so much a head.

clue.text: Regret chaps being trapped in lavatory

indicators.note: someone trapped in a room is enclosed within it, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: LAT is short for latrine, a lavatory
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Some men are sorry to have been locked in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: LAT is a crossword abbreviation for latrine.
explanation.definitionFit: To lament is to mourn or express sorrow, so to regret something deeply.

clue.text: Like some logs inane pair chopped up

indicators.note: something chopped up is cut into pieces that can be put back in any order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A silly couple chopping firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: The logs are not firewood but logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Napierian logarithms, named after John Napier, are natural logarithms to base e.

clue.text: Insult inadequate team turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the letters read from bottom to top
inadequate means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a team is a side

explanation.surface: Insulting a poor team that has bothered to show up.
explanation.walkthrough: SIDE drops its E, and SID is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is slang for showing disrespect, that is to insult or put down someone.

clue.text: Occupant of No 10 has measure introduced, that measure bringing confusion

indicators.note: having something introduced means it is put inside, so the measure goes into the occupant

parts.note: 10 Downing Street is the home of the Prime Minister
an ell is an old measure of cloth length
the same measure again

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister brings in a new measure, and chaos follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' reads as a political policy, but it is the old length ELL, used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Pell-mell, as a noun, is a confused jumble or disorderly rush.

clue.text: Rising hesitation over time of spiritual discipline? Give in!

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above the next part
rising in a down entry means the letters climb upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation
Lent is the Christian season of fasting and self-denial

explanation.surface: Growing doubt about a season of self-denial, and an urge to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'rising' turns letters upwards and 'over' puts one part on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and yield, which is to give in.

clue.text: Custom of pair sitting on deer

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting on means placed above the following part

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair
the axis or chital is a spotted Asian deer

explanation.surface: Describing the habit of a couple who sit on a deer.
explanation.walkthrough: The axis deer, or chital, is a spotted deer of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Praxis is established practice or custom, as opposed to theory.

clue.text: Attack short road, given external cover

indicators.note: something given external cover is wrapped from outside, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: a hat covers the head
AVE is the short form of avenue

explanation.surface: An assault on a short road that has been roofed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'External cover' does double duty: it signals the wrapping and supplies the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Have at is an old call or verb phrase meaning to set upon or assault someone.

clue.text: Old companion's terror being heard

indicators.note: being heard means the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: terror is fear

explanation.surface: An old friend's dread is plain to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Feer, also fere, is an archaic word for a mate or companion, used by Spenser.

clue.text: Somehow carried, being favoured by members

parts.note: in, as in fashion, means popular or favoured
members are limbs, such as arms

explanation.surface: Carried along somehow, being preferred by club members.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening adverb is not an anagram signal: it belongs to the definition, which means carried in a particular way, as a baby is.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby in arms is held and carried in someone's arms, one way of being carried.

clue.text: Friend's quietly taken aback by this insect

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: taken aback suggests being pushed backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a friend is an ally, with the possessive s

explanation.surface: A friend is quietly startled by a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as surprised, but it turns the friend's letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: Psylla is a genus of jumping plant lice, small sap-sucking insects.

clue.text: Draw out as train that's lost a little time

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so those letters drop out of the word

parts.note: to train is to educate
a as written plus T, the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Pulling out as a train runs a little behind schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a verb, to educate, not a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to bring out or develop something latent, the same Latin root as educate.

clue.text: It's easy to get two lines crossing in a mathematical figure

parts.note: something easy is simple
two crossing strokes form the letter X

explanation.surface: Drawing two intersecting lines in a geometry diagram is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A simplex is the simplest geometric figure in a given number of dimensions, such as a triangle or tetrahedron.

clue.text: Elite sets, somehow most resolute

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are arranged in another order

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The top groups are, one way or another, the most determined.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely means hard and unbending in will, so the steeliest are the most determined.

clue.text: Trifling in talk, with change in sound

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second

parts.note: a ping is a short ringing sound
to change is to alter

explanation.surface: Idle chatter that alters the way it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifling in talk' is the whole definition, matching Chambers' wording for palter.
explanation.definitionFit: To palter is to talk insincerely or trifle in speech, so paltering is shuffling, evasive chatter.

clue.text: Worker in bar is one guilty of financial misconduct

indicators.note: in places the worker inside the bar

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise
the worker ant is a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A barman turns out to be a fraudster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but it is a lever.
explanation.definitionFit: A levanter is someone who absconds without paying debts, especially gambling debts.

clue.text: Food spread very minimally, say — last thing for the little kid?

indicators.note: minimally means taking as little as possible, so only the first letter stays

parts.note: just the opening letter
e.g. means for example, or say

indicators.note: the last thing of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A sandwich paste spread very thinly, as the last treat for a toddler.
explanation.walkthrough: Vegemite is the Australian yeast-extract spread, a cousin of Marmite.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegemite is a brand of savoury yeast-extract spread eaten on toast.

clue.text: Suffers again in respect of rented flats?

parts.note: re means concerning, in respect of
a let is a property rented out

explanation.surface: A landlord suffers all over again over the flats rented out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffers' is the old sense of permitting, as in 'suffer the little children'. The question mark admits the wordplay pieces are loosely joined.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer in the old sense is to allow or let, so to suffer again is to relet.

clue.text: Government that's bad for emigre

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are put in a different order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A government that treats people who have left the country badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is a system of government, often an authoritarian one.

clue.text: Despicable person possesses horse-drawn carriages

parts.note: a rat is a low, treacherous person
to possess is to have

explanation.surface: A rotter who owns a fleet of carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratha is an Indian carriage or chariot, drawn by horses or oxen.

clue.text: Around a lake to the north I see strange trees

indicators.note: in a down entry, going to the north means reading upwards
around means surrounding, so one part wraps the other
strange means odd, so the letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Travelling north round a lake, someone spots some unusual trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' tells the jumbled letters of the last two words to wrap the upturned lake letters, while 'to the north' works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaeis is the genus of oil palms, trees grown for palm oil.

clue.text: Magistrate's essential self as money-grabber

indicators.note: a grabber seizes and holds something, so one word clutches the other inside it

parts.note: atman is the Hindu term for the soul or true self
M is an abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: A judge whose true nature is that of a greedy money-grubber.
explanation.walkthrough: ATMAN, the Hindu soul, takes M after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An amtman is a district magistrate or bailiff in Germany and Scandinavia.

clue.text: Whale getting about — explosive disturbance in water

parts.note: the sei is a species of rorqual whale
c, circa, means about
HE stands for high explosive

explanation.surface: A whale caught near an explosion churns up the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seiche is a standing-wave oscillation of the water surface in a lake or bay.

clue.text: Little monster meeting dear Parisian is one to make an impression

parts.note: ET is the small alien of the Spielberg film
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: A cute alien meets a French sweetheart and wows them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make an impression' sounds like charming someone, but an etcher literally cuts impressions into a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: An etcher bites designs into metal plates from which prints, or impressions, are taken.

clue.text: Female, ineffective hindrance, not much of an old lover?

definitions.text: not much of an old lover?

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female
a lame excuse is a feeble, ineffective one
let is an old word for obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A woman as a weak obstacle, hardly a former sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: An old lover is an old flame; a small flame is a flamelet, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamelet is a tiny flame, and a flame is slang for a sweetheart, so a little flame plays on a minor romance.

clue.text: Monkey with home county boundary

parts.note: the River Tamar forms most of the border between Cornwall and Devon
at home means in

explanation.surface: A monkey kept at a house on a county border.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river dividing the English counties of Cornwall and Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: A tamarin is a small South American monkey related to the marmosets.

clue.text: Old city's heavenly circle exuding power

indicators.note: exuding means giving off or letting out, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: a tropic is a circle of latitude, defined by the sun's position in the heavens
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: An ancient city glows with a heavenly halo of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Troic means relating to Troy, the ancient city, so it answers the possessive 'old city's'.

clue.text: The man elected that is "duff"

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
a candidate who is elected gets in
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: The winning candidate turns out to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duff' looks like British slang for useless, but it is the American slang noun for the backside. 'That' takes the following 'is' to make i.e., leaving no link.
explanation.definitionFit: Heinie and duff are both American slang for the buttocks.

clue.text: Fish making journey, heading off

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a ride is a journey

explanation.surface: A fish sets off on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide, or orfe, is a freshwater fish of the carp family.

clue.text: Dirty second child kept outside old peasant commune

indicators.note: kept outside means surrounding, so these letters go round the next part

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
CH is the abbreviation for child
a mir was a Russian village commune before the revolution

explanation.surface: A grubby younger child is shut out of an old farming community.
explanation.walkthrough: The second and the child are both abbreviations, and together they wrap round the Russian commune.
explanation.definitionFit: To smirch is to soil or stain, so to make dirty; it is the root of besmirch.

clue.text: Demigod, excellent when leading union

indicators.note: leading means going in front, so this part comes first

parts.note: A1 means excellent, with the 1 read as I
TU is the abbreviation for trade union

explanation.surface: A demigod who is excellent at heading a union.
explanation.definitionFit: An aitu is a Polynesian spirit or demigod.

clue.text: Sleeve of hair for children to wear

indicators.note: something worn is put on around another, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a mane is a head of hair
CH is the abbreviation for children

explanation.surface: A sleeve of hair for children to wear as a costume.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has the children wearing the hair, but cryptically the hair is worn around the children.
explanation.definitionFit: A manche is a heraldic sleeve with long hanging ends, used as a charge on shields.

clue.text: Let garden go wild? One sorts out knotty problem

indicators.note: to go wild is to run out of control, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Letting the garden run wild leaves a tangled mess to sort out.
explanation.walkthrough: The knotty problem is literal: tangled hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A detangler is a hair product or comb that removes knots, so it literally sorts out knots.
